title: Continuity of etale sections for sheaves of sets
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set, let $(X_i,f_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ be an inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, and let $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ with projections $f_i:X\to X_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix a stage $0\in I$ and index all subsequent stage objects and the section colimit by the cofinal upper tail $I_{\ge0}=\{i\in I:0\le i\}$. Let $G$ be a sheaf of sets on $(X_0)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Let $W_0\to X_0$ be etale and of finite presentation, put $W_i=W_0\times_{X_0}X_i$ and $W=W_0\times_{X_0}X$, and write $\rho_{i'i}:(f_{i0}^{-1}G)(W_i)\to(f_{i'0}^{-1}G)(W_{i'})$ for the transition map obtained from the unit of inverse image, the composition isomorphism $c$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and restriction along the canonical iterated-fibre-product isomorphism. Then $\rho_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{i''i'}\circ\rho_{i'i}=\rho_{i''i}$, and the canonical map $$\varinjlim_i(f_{i0}^{-1}G)(W_i)\;\longrightarrow\;(f_0^{-1}G)(W)$$ is a bijection. In particular, for the etale projection $\operatorname{pr}_i:W_i\to X_i$, restriction identifies $(\operatorname{pr}_i^{-1}f_{i0}^{-1}G)(W_i)$ with $(f_{i0}^{-1}G)(W_i)$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit), degree zero for sheaves of sets; proof via Tags 0EYL, 04HR, 09YN and the finite affine-cover reduction for qcqs schemes

proof.text: First treat the case that $W_0$ is affine (the $X_i$ remain arbitrary quasi-compact and quasi-separated). The transition morphisms $f_{i'i}$, including $f_{i0}$, are affine by hypothesis, and the projections $f_i$, including $f_0$, are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]; hence every application of the affine inverse-image comparison below has an affine morphism. The affine etale-site colimit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-colimit] supplies the cofiltered system of affine etale sites, its strictification $\mathcal C_i$, and the colimit description of the affine etale site at the limit. Restrict the sheaves $F_i=(f_{i0}^{-1}G)|_{aff}$ and their unit-induced maps along the equivalences $e_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-sheaf-transport]. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-sets-affine-etale-inverse-image-comparison] identifies these transported inverse images and units with the restrictions of the full-site inverse images, compatibly with the composition isomorphisms $c$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Since all transition maps in this system are isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle condition, [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram] identifies $\varinjlim_i g_i^{-1}F_i$ with $(f_0^{-1}G)|_{aff}$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit), proof, affine reduction via Lemma Tag 0EYL and the sets comparison inside the proof via Topologies Tag 04HR

proof.text: For an affine etale object $W_i$ descended from $W_0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites-sections] to the transported system from step 1. It gives a bijection from the filtered colimit of the stage sections to the section over the colimit object. Under the comparison of step 1, the component for $a:i'\to i$ is obtained from the unit of $g_a^{-1}\dashv g_{a*}$ by the unit clause of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-affine-etale-inverse-image-comparison], and then from clause (0) and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] together with the canonical iterated-fibre-product identification. Thus the component is exactly the transition map $\rho_{i'i}$ in the statement.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit), proof, application of Lemma Tag 09YN to an affine etale object

proof.text: For general $X_i$ and $W_0$, choose a finite affine etale covering $\{V_b\to W_0\}_{b\in B}$ with quasi-compact pairwise fibre products by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings]. For every pair $b,b'$, choose a finite affine etale covering $\{V_{bb'c}\to V_b\times_{W_0}V_{b'}\}_c$ of the quasi-compact overlap. Base change along each affine $X_i\to X_0$ gives affine objects $V_{b,i}$ and $V_{bb'c,i}$ which still form coverings at every stage and at the limit. By the sheaf condition [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition], sections over $W_i$ are the equalizer of $\prod_bF_i(V_{b,i})\rightrightarrows\prod_{b,b',c}F_i(V_{bb'c,i})$; the same equalizer description holds for sections over $W$, using the cover $\{V_b\}$ and, for injectivity, the refinements $\{V_{bb'c}\}$. The affine comparison of steps 1--2 applies to every $V_b$ and $V_{bb'c}$, and the $\rho$ maps commute with restrictions by clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] commutes the filtered colimit with these finite products and equalizers, yielding the required bijection.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit), proof, finite-cover descent from the affine case; Sites Lemma Tag 0738 for finite-cover section equalizers

proof.text: The identity and composition laws for the maps $\rho$ follow from the unit and associativity clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] and the associativity of the canonical iterated-fibre-product identifications. Thus the maps form the asserted directed system, and the bijection of step 3 is the canonical map in the statement. For the etale projection $W_i\to X_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies inverse-image sections with ordinary sections on $W_i$, giving the final assertion.

statement_change.what: The original statement uses a stage 0 and the morphisms f_{i0} for every i without choosing 0 in I or restricting to i >= 0. A general directed set has no distinguished least element; when i is not >= 0, f_{i0} is not defined. Choose a stage and use its cofinal upper tail, as in the source limit/base-change construction. This makes the intended objects well typed without requiring I to have a least element.
